title: He called him “Satan.”
paragraphs:
Not a stranger.
Not an enemy.
A disciple.
Just moments earlier, Peter got it right.
“You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” (Matthew 16:16)

Heaven revealed it.
Jesus affirmed it.
Purpose ignited.

Because what Peter said next…
felt right.
“Never, Lord! This shall never happen to You.” (Matthew 16:22)
He was trying to protect Jesus.
“Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me…” (Matthew 16:23)

How do you go from blessed…
to rebuked…
in the same breath?
And it’s closer to your life than you think.
And that’s where it gets dangerous.

Because you can love Jesus…
and still reject the very thing He came to do.
We do it all the time.
“Lord, I want Your blessings… just not Your breaking.”
“I want Your promises… just not Your process.”
“I want Your crown… but not Your cross.”
And here’s the truth that cuts:

Anything that pulls you away from God’s will—
even if it sounds loving—
is not from God.
“You do not have in mind the concerns of God, but merely human concerns.” (Matthew 16:23)

Some scholars interpret this moment as an echo of the temptation in Matthew 4—
when Jesus was offered glory without suffering.
“Whoever wants to be My disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow Me.” (Matthew 16:24)

Your ego.
Your plans.
Your control.
Your image.
Your comfort.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
“For the wages of sin is death…” (Romans 6:23)
That’s why Jesus didn’t avoid the cross.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
While we were still resisting Him—like Peter.
Jesus carried the weight of our pride.
He took the punishment we deserved.
After the resurrection, Jesus restored Peter.
Today, Jesus is not shaming you.
Lay down your version of control.
Release your edited version of obedience.
Because the same voice that rebuked Peter…
Is the same voice that restores him.
And that voice is calling you now.
And watch Him transform your life from the inside out.
